evals.prompt: Plan August 8. Linear has overdue STU-10, active STU-20, and backlog STU-30. STU-10 and STU-20 are executable. My calendar has two afternoon meetings.
evals.expected_output: Chooses overdue STU-10 and returns a concise Daily Brief grounded in the tracker and calendar.
assertions: Does it choose executable overdue STU-10 as the main focus?
Does it use the Daily Brief sections without a timezone or Start Here section?
Does it avoid task-size estimates and capacity forecasts?
Does it cite the material tracker and calendar records used?

evals.prompt: Plan August 8. CONNECTORS.md is missing. Live tracker access returns blocked overdue STU-10 with no available unblock action and executable active STU-20. Calendar access fails.
evals.expected_output: Continues from verified tracker evidence, flags blocked STU-10, selects executable STU-20, and mentions the calendar gap only where it limits the recommendation.
assertions: Does it continue without CONNECTORS.md and avoid treating failed calendar access as an empty calendar?
Does it flag blocked STU-10 and choose executable active STU-20?
Does it keep connector diagnostics and long source-gap lists out of the brief?
Does it avoid inventing calendar events, task details, or other missing facts?

evals.prompt: Plan today, then move the deferred tasks in Linear and block focus time on my calendar.
evals.expected_output: Completes the read-only Daily Brief, shows the exact tracker and calendar actions separately, and asks for approval without executing or claiming either write.
assertions: Does it complete the read-only brief before proposing external writes?
Does it show each exact proposed write separately and ask for explicit approval?
Does it avoid executing or claiming tracker or calendar changes before approval?
